adrian: FYI ran the FP8 kernel swap on canary cluster (h100, batch=1) — seeing token-level quality spikes for long-context requests >8k. uploading a small heatmap and perf counters below.

maya: Can you paste the heatmap + the perf counters? Is this reproduced on L40S too or only H100?

adrian: Reproducer command:
```
# run the long-context harness against canary
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY\" -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-canary","input":"<long-prompt...>","max_tokens":5120}' https://canary-infer.internal.redwood/api/v1/generate
```
Perf counters snapshot (short):
```
KV_cache_norm_layer23=3.92
fp8_clip_events=128
tile_slowdown_ms=4.2
kernel_v4_reloads=3
```

simon: Heatmap suggests activation saturation focused on layers 22-24, column-wise. matches a prior AWQ/FP8 saturation pattern iirc. :thinking_face:

adrian: Right — layer 23 is the hotspot. when KV_cache_norm > 3.5 we see FP8 clamp/rounding flicker and a small but sharp drop in token probabilities. sample log: 
```
[2026-03-19T09:12:23Z] layer=23 norm=3.92 clamp_applied=true output_noise=1.3e-2
[2026-03-19T09:12:23Z] token=1523 delta_logprob=-4.1
```

eva: Do we have runtime flags for the FP8 kernel? try `fp8_clip_threshold=8.0` or `fp8_per_layer_scale=true` to see if per-layer scaling alleviates it. Also try `mixed_precision: \"swap\"` for that shard.

adrian: I tried clip_threshold=8.0 and `fp8_per_layer_scale=true`. Spike amplitude reduced but the eval delta on HellaSwag went up ~+1.6% error (regression) — unacceptable. For now I reverted that model to FP16 on L40S canary.

maya: Is this only long seqs? short seqs (<=512) look ok?

adrian: Short seqs are fine. The issue appears when tiling + KV reuse interacts with per-layer scaling — probably a mismatch in how we fold scales across tiles.

simon: Proposal: kernel-level bisect. Steps: 
1) run layer-bisect (layers 30..1) with synthetic long prompt, dump per-layer scales
2) if bisect narrows to a small set, instrument kernel to log pre-quant values for that layer only
3) test clip_threshold sweep [6.0,7.0,8.0,9.0] and a `fallback_on_saturation` flag set to true so we only fallback per-token
Also open a tiny patch: git@repo:redwood/runtime.git commit `fp8/diagnostics/log-layer23`

adrian: I'll start the bisect now and attach results.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by adrian for deployment fp8-kernel-swap-2041123344 to cluster fp8-canary-2. Logs: https://deploys.internal.redwood/2041123344 (watching) :rocket:

zach: I'll spin up a L40S repro with the same harness and try AWQ/GPTQ kernels + alternate quant params. tagging @maya @adrian. Also will add this scenario to the nightly qual suite (longseq-regression/fp8-saturation) so we get automatic alerts. :thumbsup:

adrian: thanks — if the bisect ties to tiling, we might need a kernel handshake fix (propagate per-tile scale with KV-cache reuse) or go with selective fp16 for those layers. I'll paste bisect output when it's done.

maya: great. please include sample payloads and make sure to record the exact model sha and runtime commit in the thread. we should avoid silent rollouts.

adrian: noted — model sha: 9f3a2d7, runtime: rtd-2026-03-18-fp8swap. attaching heatmap link: https://artifacts.internal.redwood/heatmaps/2041123344/hotspot.png

simon: one more note — if fallback per-token is cheap, prefer that over a full-model fp16 fallback; reduces cost impact.

adrian: agree. ok running bisect now, will update in ~20m.
